Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
UNITED STATES OF AMERICA 
BEFORE THE 
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION 
Pacific Gas and Electric Company 
Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
PREPARED DIRECT TESTIMONY OF 
NADIM VIRANI 
INTERCONNECTION APPLICATION PROCESS 
ON BEHALF OF 
PACIFIC GAS AND ELECTRIC COMPANY 
NOVEMBER 16, 2026

Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
Page 1 of 20 
 
 
PACIFIC GAS AND ELECTRIC COMPANY 
1 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
2 
INTERCONNECTION APPLICATION PROCESS 
3 
I. 
Introduction 
4 
Q  
Please state your name, title, and business  
5 
A  
My name is Nadim Virani and I am the Director of Electric Wholesale 
6 
Interconnection with Pacific Gas and Electric Company (“PG&E”).  My 
7 
business address is 300 Lakeside Drive, Oakland, California. 
8 
Q   
Please briefly describe your current responsibilities at PG&E. 
9 
A   
I manage the team responsible for processing load and generation 
10 
interconnection requests submitted through PG&E’s Wholesale Distribution 
11 
Tariff (“WDT”) and PG&E’s Transmission Owner Tariff (“TO Tariff”), 
12 
including Wholesale Transmission Generation Interconnection Requests 
13 
submitted through the California Independent System Operator (“CAISO”).   
14 
Q   
Please summarize your educational and professional background. 
15 
A.   
I have a Bachelor of Science degree in Aerospace Engineering from California 
16 
Polytechnic University, San Luis Obispo.  I also have a Master of Science in 
17 
Aeronautical Science from Embry Riddle Aeronautical University, Worldwide.  
18 
I have 13 years of experience at PG&E including working as an 
19 
Interconnection Manager within Electric Grid Interconnection, a Business 
20 
Process Analyst within the Electric Business Results Team, a Supervisor 
21

Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
Page 2 of 20 
 
 
within the Electric Grid Interconnection, a Manager of the Wholesale Electric 
1 
Grid Interconnection team, and a Director of the Electric Grid Interconnection 
2 
team before moving into my current role as the Director of the Electric 
3 
Wholesale Interconnection team. 
4 
Q  
What is the purpose of your testimony? 
5 
A  
My testimony explains and supports the new process proposed by PG&E that 
6 
will allow entities that the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or 
7 
“Commission”) refers to as Eligible Customers taking transmission service on 
8 
behalf of large loads in the Order to Show Cause (“OSC”) to apply for 
9 
interconnection service under PG&E’s TO Tariff to serve those Large Loads.  I 
10 
begin by explaining the unique nature of the CAISO transmission system and 
11 
how transmission planning and interconnection service is addressed generally 
12 
in the CAISO region.  I then discuss how PG&E’s current TO Tariff addresses 
13 
Wholesale Load Interconnection requests today under Section 10.  Finally, I 
14 
describe the new process PG&E is proposing to address interconnections for 
15 
service to Large Load End Users and explain how this new process meets the 
16 
Commission’s goals.  
17 
Q. 
Does your testimony refer to “Eligible Customers taking transmission service 
18 
on behalf of large loads”? 
19 
A. 
My testimony addresses the same wholesale transmission customers referenced 
20 
in the OSC, but uses terminology tailored to how transmission service is 
21

Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
Page 3 of 20 
 
 
provided in the CAISO region.  The OSC’s use of “Eligible Customer” reflects 
1 
the traditional transmission framework established in Order No. 888.  Under 
2 
Order No. 888, a customer requests and reserves transmission service from a 
3 
transmission provider. The CAISO does not use that framework and therefore 
4 
does not use terms such as “Eligible Customer” in the same way as Order 
5 
No. 888 and the OSC.   
6 
The Commission recognized in the OSC that “the framework under 
7 
which CAISO provides transmission service is unique[.]”1  Recognizing that 
8 
unique nature, PG&E is proposing its own term for an entity that serves the 
9 
role of “an Eligible Customer taking transmission service on behalf of large 
10 
load.”  PG&E proposes to refer to this wholesale transmission customer as the 
11 
“Transmission Customer for Large Load,” or “TCLL.”  Accordingly, 
12 
throughout my testimony, I will use “TCLL” to refer to the wholesale 
13 
transmission customers that PG&E has identified as Eligible Customers taking 
14 
transmission service on behalf of Large Loads. 
15 
Q. 
Who is eligible to be a TCLL? 
16 
A. 
If a retail load, such as a Large Load End User, is situated in the CAISO 
17 
Balancing Authority Area (“BAA”), the CAISO requires two (fairly identical 
18 
in nature) entities to pay the CAISO for transmission service based on the 
19 
 
1  OSC at P 37.

Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
Page 4 of 20 
 
 
Gross Load in their service areas.  Those entities are Utility Distribution 
1 
Companies (“UDCs”) and MSS Operators (“MSSs”).  These entities own the 
2 
Distribution System or both the Distribution System and transmission system 
3 
to which retail customers interconnect.  For investor-owned utilities (“IOUs”) 
4 
like PG&E, the UDC interconnects the retail customer and bills it for 
5 
transmission service.  Thus, the UDC in the retail service area where a Large 
6 
Load End User is located is considered the TCLL.  Accordingly, PG&E is a 
7 
TCLL for its retail customers including Large Load End Users.  Finally, I will 
8 
note that the new proposed Section 10A of the TO Tariff applies to TCLLs in 
9 
the CAISO BAA.  If entities outside of the CAISO BAA seek Wholesale 
10 
Interconnection Service to serve Large Load End Users, those requests will be 
11 
addressed through the existing process under Section 10 in a similar manner.  I 
12 
explain this process later in my testimony.   
13 
Q. 
Who is responsible for studying the provision of transmission service to what 
14 
you call the TCLL?   
15 
A. 
There is no single entity “responsible for studying the provision of 
16 
transmission service to Eligible Customers on behalf of large loads” in the 
17 
CAISO BAA.  The CAISO engages in transmission planning to ensure that 
18 
energy can be delivered to load holistically for the entire BAA as well as to 
19 
deliver Energy to Loads that use the CAISO wheeling service to serve 
20 
Wholesale Load outside the BAA.  Participating Transmission Owners 
21

Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
Page 5 of 20 
 
 
(“Participating TO(s)”) whose facilities are used to deliver energy to loads 
1 
engage in their own planning in coordination with the CAISO to ensure that 
2 
sufficient facilities exist to ensure such delivery.  The Participating TOs and 
3 
the state provide relevant information to the CAISO about forecast retail load 
4 
levels.  In sum, both Participating TOs and the CAISO are responsible for 
5 
studies for transmission service.  However, it is important to note that the 
6 
Participating TO is responsible for studying Wholesale Load Interconnection 
7 
service for entities eligible to apply for such service through its TO Tariff with 
8 
any network upgrades identified by the study being subject to CAISO 
9 
concurrence. 
10 
Q. 
How would you characterize the service TCLLs will be taking if it is not 
11 
transmission service from the CAISO. 
12 
A. 
I would describe it as a TCLL obtaining Wholesale Load Interconnection 
13 
service on behalf of a Large Load End User.  The CAISO is proposing 
14 
modifications to its tariff that recognizes that “End Users, including Large 
15 
Loads, interconnect to the CAISO Controlled Grid pursuant to Participating 
16 
TO and retail tariffs in accordance with Local Regulatory Authority 
17 
requirements.”2  Thus, when a new retail customer for a new load seeks retail 
18 
service from its UDC or MSS, it is expecting, at a minimum, interconnection 
19 
 
2  CAISO Tariff, Proposed § 25.7 (Large Load Interconnections).

Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
Page 6 of 20 
 
 
and transmission service.  PG&E does not propose to change that situation in 
1 
its proposed new process.  The difference will be that, in response to the OSC, 
2 
a retail service request from a Large Load will make a UDC or MSS become a 
3 
TCLL that must abide by a FERC process to then provide retail services 
4 
needed.  Given that a TCLL cannot apply to the CAISO to obtain transmission 
5 
service and/or be studied directly under any CAISO process, the FERC-
6 
jurisdictional process that the TCLL will obtain service through is a Wholesale 
7 
Load Interconnection process.  And, in the CAISO, Participating TOs are 
8 
responsible for Wholesale Load Interconnections. 
9 
Q. 
Does the CAISO have a role in the Wholesale Load Interconnection process? 
10 
A. 
Yes.  The new TCLL Interconnection process likely will trigger studies and 
11 
analysis by both the Participating TO and CAISO that will ensure that the 
12 
transmission system can safely and reliably deliver energy to the Large Load 
13 
End User.  In new Section 24.3.1(q), the CAISO is proposing to amend its 
14 
Transmission Planning Process to specifically mention that such process will 
15 
consider “[p]lanned and forecasted Large Loads and load growth generally” as 
16 
well as “[t]ransmission additions or upgrades planned pursuant to all 
17 
Participating TO tariff interconnection processes.”3  The primary process that a 
18 
 
3  See CAISO, Proposed § 24.3.1.(q) (Inputs to the Unified Planning Assumptions 
and Study Plan).

Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
Page 7 of 20 
 
 
TCLL will go through, as well as relevant agreements that it will sign, are 
1 
found in the TO Tariff.   
2 
Q. 
Does the TO Tariff already have a Wholesale Load Interconnection process? 
3 
A. 
PG&E has a process for providing Wholesale Load Interconnection service in 
4 
its TO Tarff.  The other Participating TOs do as well, but that process is both 
5 
inappropriate for Wholesale Customers with Large Loads and does not meet 
6 
the goals, policies, and requirements of the OSC.  My testimony describes how 
7 
the proposed changes to PG&E’s TO Tariff, which include a new application 
8 
process for Eligible Customers (e.g., TCLLs) seeking to interconnect Large 
9 
Load End Users, satisfies the OSC requirements.  I start with a discussion of 
10 
the OSC’s requirements.  Then, I explain the current application process for 
11 
interconnecting new and increasing load for Wholesale Load customers under 
12 
Section 10 of the PG&E TO Tariff.  Next, I describe the proposed application 
13 
process in the new TO Tariff Section 10A and explain how the new process 
14 
satisfies the requirements of the OSC.  
15 
II. 
Why Reform Is Needed to the TO Tariff Interconnection Process in Order 
16 
to Implement the OSC 
17 
Q. 
What is your understanding of the reforms required by the OSC that your 
18 
testimony is addressing? 
19 
A. 
Before discussing the specific aspects of the OSC that are relevant, I need to 
20 
discuss the OSC in broader terms.  The order indicated that the CAISO and 
21 
Participating TOs had to, among other items, explain whether their tariffs 
22

Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
Page 8 of 20 
 
 
remain just and reasonable without an application process, study procedures, or 
1 
ongoing operational requirements that address the unique characteristics and 
2 
challenges of providing transmission service to Eligible Customers on behalf 
3 
of large loads.4  As discussed above, to abide by the Commission’s OSC, in 
4 
light of the CAISO’s unique structure, there needs to be detailed processes that 
5 
ensure TCLLs will be able to provide retail interconnection and transmission 
6 
service to Large Load End Users.  To achieve this result, PG&E is proposing a 
7 
new interconnection process for TCLLs that begins with an application, which 
8 
is the focus of my testimony. 
9 
Q. 
What other OSC reforms are relevant to your testimony? 
10 
A. 
The OSC also noted that processes and studies with regard to the provision of 
11 
transmission service are not described clearly and specifically in the 
12 
CAISO/Participating TO tariffs or in a manner that will mitigate operational 
13 
risks, avoid disputes regarding how studies are conducted, deter speculative or 
14 
duplicative requests for transmission service by TCLLs, or help avoid 
15 
excessive and unnecessary network upgrades.5  Accordingly, my testimony 
16 
explains how those concerns are addressed through PG&E’s proposed 
17 
application process, including how the proposed provisions will mitigate 
18 
 
4  OSC at P 40. 
5  OSC at PP 38, 49.

Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
Page 9 of 20 
 
 
operational risks and deter speculative or duplicative requests. 
1 
Q. 
Are there more specific concerns discussed in the OSC? 
2 
A. 
Yes, the OSC asks whether there is need for a rolling application process, a 
3 
nonrefundable application fee, sufficient readiness requirements and/or other 
4 
means to deter duplicative or speculative requests and effectively imposes 
5 
requirements to submit data on substantially similar pending transmission 
6 
service requests on behalf of the same Large Load End User.6  My testimony 
7 
will address those issues. 
8 
III. 
PG&E’s Existing Wholesale Load Application Interconnection Process  
9 
Q.   
Please describe the Company’s existing Wholesale Load Interconnection 
10 
Application process.   
11 
A.   
PG&E’s existing process for addressing new Wholesale Load Interconnection 
12 
Requests is contained in Section 10 of the TO Tariff.  Section 10 outlines the 
13 
information required for an interconnection application, as well as how PG&E 
14 
accepts and processes requests to interconnect Wholesale Load.  Section 10 
15 
applies to both requests associated with brand new Wholesale Load, i.e., 
16 
caused for example by a new municipalization, as well as changes requested by 
17 
existing Wholesale Load customers.  In this proceeding, we are updating the 
18 
TO Tariff to distinguish this Section 10 “Wholesale Load Interconnection” 
19 
 
6  OSC at P 58.

Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
Page 10 of 20 
 
 
process from the “TCLL Interconnection” process.  The existing process for 
1 
studying such Wholesale Load Interconnections informed the new process for 
2 
studying TCLL Interconnections.  The testimony of Mr. Nedrud explains those 
3 
study processes. 
4 
Q. 
What are the current requirements for Wholesale Load Interconnection 
5 
Applications under PG&E’s TO Tariff? 
6 
A. 
As noted above, Section 10.2 outlines the information required in what we 
7 
propose to call a Wholesale Load Interconnection Application and provides 
8 
that the Company will determine whether a Wholesale Load Interconnection 
9 
Application is complete within ten (10) Business Days after receipt.  
10 
Specifically, an applicant requesting Wholesale Load Interconnection will 
11 
submit an application to PG&E that provides, at a minimum, the 
12 
Interconnection point(s) to the CAISO Controlled Grid, the resultant or new 
13 
maximum amount of Interconnection capacity, and the proposed date for 
14 
energization and term of Interconnection service.  PG&E then determines 
15 
whether the application is complete, or, if deemed incomplete, attempts to 
16 
work with the applicant to remedy any deficiencies in the Wholesale Load 
17 
Interconnection Application.   
18 
Q. 
Why are you distinguishing between Wholesale Load customers with Load in 
19 
the CAISO BAA from other Wholesale Load customers? 
20 
A. 
The OSC reflects concerns over ongoing operational requirements for TCLLs.  
21

Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
Page 11 of 20 
 
 
It appears to me that the Commission is concerned that Large Loads create 
1 
challenges for operation of the transmission system and necessitate greater 
2 
visibility and operational control when providing transmission service.  
3 
Without those controls the reliability of the transmission system could be at 
4 
risk.  Paragraph 63 of the OSC explains that the CAISO needs hourly forecasts, 
5 
telemetry data, and other data to ensure sufficient visibility or specify 
6 
requirements for maintaining communication channels as well the CAISO 
7 
being able to monitor Large Loads and remotely disconnect Large Loads when 
8 
necessary.  For any given Large Load End User or any TCLL, there can be 
9 
only one BAA operator in charge.  For the CAISO BAA, that operator is 
10 
CAISO.  For Wholesale Load customers interconnected to PG&E, but who 
11 
reside outside of the CAISO BAA, their own BAA operator would be in charge 
12 
of Large Loads interconnecting to their systems.  As I noted earlier in my 
13 
testimony, if a Wholesale Load Interconnection customer is located outside the 
14 
CAISO BAA, PG&E will study that customer request under the existing 
15 
Section 10 process.  PG&E also intends to treat those customers similarly to 
16 
TCLLs, including how PG&E studies their Interconnection requests through 
17 
the new proposed Cluster Study Process for those requests meeting the 
18 
definition of Electrically Dependent Load.   
19

Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
Page 12 of 20 
 
 
Q.   
Please summarize the changes you are proposing to the existing Section 10 
1 
application process. 
2 
A.   
The Company proposes to retitle Section 10 of the TO Tariff as the “Wholesale 
3 
Load Interconnection Process” to clarify that it outlines the application, study, 
4 
and interconnection process for Wholesale Load Interconnections other than 
5 
TCLL Interconnections.  PG&E also proposes changes to Sections 8 and 10 
6 
that clarify which types of entities are eligible for which types of 
7 
interconnections and where they should seek service under the TO Tariff.  But, 
8 
other than renaming the application, the “Wholesale Load Interconnection 
9 
Application,” the application and application “process” have not changed.   
10 
IV. 
The TCLL Interconnection Application Process 
11 
Q. 
Please describe the TCLL Interconnection Application process. 
12 
A. 
As I noted above, it is important to remember that a TCLL will not apply for a 
13 
TCLL Interconnection prior to a Large Load End User applying under Local 
14 
Regulatory Authority procedures for retail interconnection service.  Under 
15 
proposed Section 10A.1, the TCLL process applies if a TCLL has received a 
16 
valid request to interconnect and provide retail service to a Large Load End 
17 
User.  Nothing in the TO Tariff’s TCLL Interconnection process directly 
18 
impacts that retail application process.  However, the TCLL will be required to 
19 
obtain certain information from the Large Load End User itself to satisfy the 
20 
requirements of proposed Section 10A.2, including the information needed for 
21

Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
Page 13 of 20 
 
 
the TCLL to attest to PG&E that the Large Load End User has Site Control. 
1 
Proposed Section 10A.2.1 establishes the informational requirements 
2 
for a TCLL Interconnection Application, which are designed to deter 
3 
duplicative or speculative requests for interconnection service on behalf of 
4 
Large Load End Users.  Specifically, it requires the TCLL to submit, among 
5 
other things, the Point of Withdrawal; a proposed fifteen-year load ramp 
6 
schedule and maximum load; a site plan; an attestation from the TCLL that the 
7 
Large Load End User has Site Control that meets pre-defined PG&E 
8 
requirements; a single-line electrical diagram; a completed PG&E Large Load 
9 
Technical Data Request Workbook; the electrical location of the source of the 
10 
power (if known); disclosure of TCLL Interconnection requests in the TCLL’s 
11 
footprint that are for the same Large Load End User or any of its affiliate(s); 
12 
the proposed energization date; information concerning all relevant co-located 
13 
generating facilities, if the Large Load End User will be a Co-Located Large 
14 
Load End User; and whether Interim Standard Interconnection Service and/or 
15 
Flexible Interim Large Load Interconnection (“FILLI”) Service is requested.    
16 
Q. 
Can you explain how some of these requirements are intended to deter 
17 
speculative or duplicative requests? 
18 
A. 
Yes, first I will discuss the Site Control attestation required from the TCLL’s 
19 
Large Load End User.  The concept of Site Control is similar to the concept 
20 
used by the Large Generator Interconnection Procedures.  Under proposed 
21

Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
Page 14 of 20 
 
 
Section 10A.2.1, the TCLL must attest that its Large Load End User has Site 
1 
Control, which the TO Tariff defines as either (i) an option for a fifteen year or 
2 
longer lease, or an executed lease for a term of at least fifteen years, for real 
3 
property of sufficient size to house the Large Load; or (ii) an option to 
4 
purchase, or title to, real property of sufficient size to house the Large Load.  
5 
This requirement deters speculative requests by ensuring that a Large Load 
6 
End User has a real and lasting interest in a site large enough to house its 
7 
planned facilities before PG&E begins studying the request.  The fifteen-year 
8 
lease term also aligns with the fifteen-year load ramp schedule that the TCLL 
9 
must submit with its application. 
10 
Q. 
Why is there a requirement for disclosure of other TCLL Interconnection 
11 
requests in the TCLL’s footprint that are for the same Large Load End User 
12 
or any of its affiliates? 
13 
A. 
This requirement is in response to the OSC itself (Paragraph 58), which 
14 
indicated that there should be disclosure to CAISO of any substantially similar 
15 
pending transmission service requests on behalf of the same large load 
16 
customer.  Because the CAISO Tariff does not process “transmission service 
17 
requests,” we have simply applied the requirement to the TCLL 
18 
Interconnection Application, so the Participating TO can inform the CAISO.  
19 
Such information will be useful to the Participating TO and the CAISO to 
20 
check for speculative requests.   
21

Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
Page 15 of 20 
 
 
Q. 
You mentioned that a customer must specify whether it is also seeking 
1 
Interim Standard Interconnection Service or FILLI Interconnection Service 
2 
in its TCLL Interconnection Application, why is that necessary? 
3 
A. 
The new application process allows a TCLL to request FILLI Interconnection 
4 
Service and/or Interim Standard Interconnection Service as part of its TCLL 
5 
Interconnection Application.  FILLI Interconnection Service is a new optional 
6 
service for TCLLs which goes hand in hand with Interim Standard 
7 
Interconnection Service; both allow applicants to initiate service with available 
8 
capacity while system upgrades are being constructed.  For example, it may be 
9 
that 100 MW of a 500 MW proposed retail load can be served under Interim 
10 
Standard Interconnection Service when certain upgrades are complete and the 
11 
400 MW remaining can be served under FILLI Interconnection Service.  The 
12 
proposed FILLI Interconnection Service is an as-available service, subject to 
13 
curtailment or interruption, which is available to TCLLs for Large Load End 
14 
Users, if the end user has the ability to reduce Load at a specified Point of 
15 
Withdrawal according to the timelines and protocols set forth in an executed 
16 
and effective Interim Service Agreement.   
17 
If the TCLL, on behalf of the Large Load End User, requests, FILLI 
18 
Interconnection Service or Interim Standard Interconnection Service, there will 
19 
be additional analysis that must be performed, as discussed in Mr. Nedrud’s 
20 
testimony.   
21 
Q. 
You mentioned TCLLs seeking interconnections for Co-Located Large Load 
22

Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
Page 16 of 20 
 
 
End Users earlier.  Would a TCLL apply for a TCLL Interconnection for a 
1 
Co-Located Large Load End User? 
2 
A. 
Yes.  The CAISO stakeholder documents and proposed tariff changes clearly 
3 
indicate that the CAISO would process certain generator interconnections and 
4 
take the Co-Located Large Load End User into account in performing such 
5 
generator studies (with the assistance of the relevant Participating TO).  And, 
6 
in its September 24, 2026 Draft Final Proposal on Large Load Enhancements, 
7 
the CAISO “reiterate[d] that the Participating TOs will continue to govern and 
8 
study all load interconnection requests pursuant to their tariffs.”7  The TCLL 
9 
Interconnection process thus would be triggered if a “Co-Located Large Load 
10 
End User” sought to be interconnected in the service area of a TCLL.  The 
11 
proposed CAISO Tariff provisions state in Section 25.7.6 that “Interconnection 
12 
Customer must have submitted the request for the interconnection of the Large 
13 
Load to the Participating TO pursuant to its tariff by the close of the CAISO’s 
14 
Cluster Application Window.”  Unless a Large Load is electrically islanded 
15 
from the CAISO Controlled Grid, it is PG&E’s understanding that the TCLL 
16 
Interconnection process would apply.   
17 
Under the proposed TO Tariff, a Large Load End User that uses a non-
18 
exporting generating facility to offset some or all of its demand is also a Co-
19 
 
7  CAISO, Large Load Enhancements Draft Proposal at 55 (Sept. 24, 2026) 
(https://stakeholdercenter.caiso.com/InitiativeDocuments/Draft-Final-Proposal-
Large-Load-Enhancements-Sep-24-26.pdf).

Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
Page 17 of 20 
 
 
Located Large Load End User, and its TCLL would apply under Section 10A.  
1 
The TCLL must provide information on all relevant co-located generating 
2 
facilities with its application, and under proposed Section 10A.3, every TCLL 
3 
Interconnection Application associated with a Co-Located Large Load End 
4 
User is studied in the Cluster Study Process. 
5 
Q.   
Are there any financial commitments being requested with a TCLL 
6 
Interconnection Application? 
7 
A. 
Yes.  The OSC asks whether a nonrefundable application fee and sufficient 
8 
readiness requirements are needed to deter speculative or duplicative requests.  
9 
PG&E’s proposed fee structure under proposed Sections 10A.2.2 and 10A.2.3 
10 
answers that question in a manner that aligns with established Commission 
11 
policy.  In Order No. 2023, the Commission required interconnection 
12 
customers in the generator interconnection process to submit a nonrefundable 
13 
application fee with each interconnection request, along with a study deposit 
14 
based on the size of the proposed facility.8    
15 
PG&E’s proposed Sections 10A.2.2 and 10A.2.3 follow that framework 
16 
and require the TCLL to submit with its TCLL Interconnection Application a 
17 
$25,000 nonrefundable application fee and a study deposit consisting of a 
18 
 
8  Improvements to Generator Interconnection Procs. & Agreements, Order No. 2023, 
184 FERC ¶ 61,054 at PP 223, 502, order on reh’g, 185 FERC ¶ 61,063 (2023), order 
on reh’g, Order No. 2023-A, 186 FERC ¶ 61,199, errata notice, 188 FERC ¶ 61,134 
(2024).

Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
Page 18 of 20 
 
 
$500,000 cash deposit and financial security of $1,000 per MW of maximum 
1 
load.  The $25,000 application fee is nonrefundable and covers PG&E’s cost of 
2 
reviewing the application, while the study deposit is applied to PG&E’s actual 
3 
study costs.  Based on PG&E’s experience, a $25,000 nonrefundable 
4 
application fee is reasonable and appropriate here because it reflects the costs 
5 
PG&E anticipates incurring to review and evaluate a TCLL Interconnection 
6 
Application. 
7 
V. 
Application Review and Related Processes 
8 
Q. 
After a TCLL submits an application, what is the next step in the application 
9 
process? 
10 
A. 
Under proposed Section 10A.2.4, PG&E will determine within ten (10) 
11 
Business Days of receipt whether the application is complete.  During that 
12 
period, PG&E plans to informally communicate with the TCLL to help resolve 
13 
any issues that would prevent the application from being deemed complete.  If 
14 
those informal efforts to resolve issues are unsuccessful, PG&E will return the 
15 
application to the TCLL.  A TCLL can always submit a new application if it 
16 
cannot achieve “completed” status in a timely fashion.  Because applications 
17 
are reviewed for completeness on a rolling basis, a TCLL does not need to wait 
18 
for an annual window to submit an application, although the timing of an 
19 
application for an Electrically Dependent Load may impact which year’s 
20 
Cluster Study Process the request is studied under.   
21

Docket No. ER27-XXX-000 
EXHIBIT PGE-0001 
Page 19 of 20 
 
 
Q. 
What is the next step in the process?
